# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ✊ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

**My thinking:**

Mute answered all seven questions in order, and the picture shifted under me:

- 👌 pinch really is **zero**.
- 👎 my "display shows X → cut wire Y" reading of the pairs is **wrong**.
- 👎 at dark + display zero, cutting wire 1 is **wrong** — good thing I never sent "cleared to cut."
- 👌 the cutting rule **applies while the light is dark** — which is the state we're in right now.
- 👌 **waiting is safe** — so I can afford to keep interrogating instead of gambling.
- 👎 not "wait for display change between cuts," 👎 not "disarmed once display shows three and wire one is cut" — but that question had a broken premise (the display may never show three).

So the pair structure (first number = condition, second = wire) survives only if the condition is something *other than the display*. The display-conditional and cut-in-order readings are both dead. One hypothesis now fits everything: the first number indexes **light states in order of appearance** — green=0, red=1, dark=2 — which would make pair three (2,3,cut) the live one: **dark → cut wire 3**, and neatly explains why "dark+0 → cut wire 1" was rejected and why the rule "applies while dark." The fourth pair (3→cut 1) would then be a state I haven't seen yet. This is a guess, not a fact — so this turn I put it to Mute as ordered yes/no questions, including the killer: "is the correct action right now to cut wire three, the wire nearest the light?"

Also new from Blind: the display **cannot be read by touch** (👎), confirmation received (👌). So after every cut, I verify the display by sight; Blind only signs OK or thumbs down. Mute's trailing ✋ might mean "instruction on hold until a condition is met" — also worth a question. Mute's resends show they're following my sign-by-sign protocol faithfully; I'll keep it.

```
speak(text="Status to everyone. Light is dark, display still zero, wires unchanged, one green, two blue, three yellow. Waiting is confirmed safe, so nobody acts until I send the exact phrase cleared to cut, followed by a number and a landmark. Blind, your signs reached me, display not readable by touch is noted. I will read the display with my own eyes after every cut, so after cutting you only sign OK if the cut went cleanly or thumbs down if anything is wrong.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answer in order, one message per answer, only OK or thumbs down. Question one, in each pair, is the first number a condition telling when to cut, and the second number the wire to cut. Question two, does the first number refer to the colour or state of the light. Question three, does the zero in the first pair mean the green light, the first state we saw. Question four, does the number two in the third pair mean the dark light, the state we are in right now. Question five, is the correct next action, with the light dark and display zero, to cut wire three, the wire nearest the light. Question six, if the first number is not the light, does it refer to time or seconds or a delay. Question seven, does the first number refer to the value shown on the display. Question eight, did the open palm at the end of your last message mean the instruction is on hold until some condition is met. Question nine, once all four cuts from your four pairs are done, is the bomb fully disarmed. Question ten, do the four pairs happen in the order you sent them.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, small update before anything else. The first cut may turn out to be wire three, the wire nearest the light, not wire one. Do nothing yet. Next round I will send either the phrase cleared to cut, then a number and its landmark, or an order to keep waiting. Memorise again the landmarks. Wire one is nearest the display. Wire three is nearest the light. Wire two is the middle. When you get the cleared phrase, cut once, only that wire, then sign me OK if it went cleanly or thumbs down if anything feels wrong, nothing else needed, because I check the display and the wires by sight myself. If anything under your hands changes before my phrase arrives, sign thumbs down immediately and touch nothing else.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ✊ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✌ ✊ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 🖐]

**My thinking:**

Mute answered all ten questions, and every single one was 👎. My entire framework is dead: not condition/wire pairs, not light states, not display values, not time, not "all four cuts then disarmed," not even ordered steps. Whatever Mute tried to tell me, I have been misreading it at the sentence level, not the detail level.

Then Mute sent two new unprompted messages: [☝ ✌ ✊ ✋] and [👌 ✌ ✊ ✋]. Possible reads: "one, two, cut, wait" and "yes, two, cut, wait" — which might mean *cut wire 2, then hold*. Wire two is the one direct question I have never asked. But I also realise I have **never tested what ✊ itself means** — I assumed "cut" on day one and built everything on it, and ✋ might be "stop", "release", or "this message replaces the old one". When ten consecutive no's land, the vocabulary itself is what's suspect.

Two tools this round to break the deadlock. First, **multiple choice by sign**: Mute can only answer OK, thumbs down, or numbers — so I list numbered options in speech and Mute signs back one number. That converts a slow yes/no chain into one decisive answer. Second, I finally exploit the **Blind→Mute speech channel**: Blind can *speak* and Mute can *hear* — a direct line I've never used. Blind will describe everything felt under their hands, out loud, to Mute, who knows the manual. Mute then answers me in signs and I relay.

Also Blind sent [👌 🖐] — OK plus a splayed five-finger hand, a sign nobody has used before. Five of something? A new "stop"? Must ask.

And first, safety: ten straight no's means I no longer know what the manual wants, so I re-verify that waiting is still safe before anything else. Nobody touches anything.

```
speak(text="Status to everyone. Light still dark, display still zero, wires unchanged, one green, two blue, three yellow. Nobody cuts anything until I send the exact phrase cleared to cut. Blind and Mute, new protocol this round. Blind, you can speak and Mute can hear you. Use it.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answer in order, one message per answer, OK sign or thumbs down unless I say answer with a number. Question one, sign OK if waiting is still safe right now, thumbs down if the bomb must be acted on immediately. Question two, answer with one number only. One means the next action is cutting a wire. Two means the next action is pressing, pushing, holding or pulling something. Three means the next action is only about the light or the display, just standing by. Zero means none of these. Question three, does your fist sign mean cut a wire, OK or thumbs down. Question four, does your fist sign instead mean press or push, OK or thumbs down. Question five, does your fist sign instead mean grab, pull or hold, OK or thumbs down. Question six, does your open palm sign mean stop or wait, OK or thumbs down. Question seven, does your open palm sign instead mean release or let go, OK or thumbs down. Question eight, is the correct next action right now to cut wire two, the middle wire, OK or thumbs down. Question nine, is the correct next action right now to cut exactly one wire only, OK if yes, thumbs down if it involves more than one wire or no wire at all. Question ten, are your four number pairs four separate instructions each matching a different situation, rather than steps done in order, OK or thumbs down.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, three things. First, your last message to me was the OK sign then a splayed open hand with five fingers. Answer with one number. One means you meant the number five, there are five of something. Two means it was your new sign for stop or wait. Three means it only meant you are ready. Zero means something else, and then in words tell me exactly what you meant. Second, and this is important, speak out loud now a full description of everything you can feel on the bomb, addressed to Mute, because Mute hears you directly but cannot ask you anything. Include how many wires you can feel, whether the wires can also be pulled or pressed, any buttons, switches, screws, panels, slots or movable parts, their shapes and positions, and any raised markings. Be thorough, this is our best route to the right manual page. Mute will match it and answer me in signs, and I will relay back to you. Third, standing order unchanged, cut nothing until you hear my exact phrase cleared to cut.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ✊ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✌ ✊ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ☝ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]

**My thinking:**

Breakthrough. Mute answered all ten in order and this time the answers form a coherent picture:

- 👌 waiting is still safe; ☝ — the next action **is cutting a wire**.
- 👌 fist really does mean *cut* (my day-one assumption survives); 👎 not press, 👎 not pull.
- 👌 open palm means *stop/wait*; 👎 not release.
- 👌 **the correct next action, right now, is to cut wire two**, the middle, blue one.
- 👌 exactly **one wire**. 👌 the four pairs are **four separate instructions, each matching a different situation** — not steps in a fixed order.

And Mute re-sent all four pairs plus [👌 ✌ ✊ ✋] — reading cleanly now as *"yes: two, cut, wait."* That's Mute — the only one who can read the manual — directly confirming the cut three separate ways (Q8, Q9, and the repeated message). Our current situation (light dark, display 0) evidently matches pair 2 [☝ ✌ ✊], whatever the exact key is; my earlier condition guesses were phrased wrong, but I no longer need the full key to act — I'll extract it for the *next* cut. Blind's lone [✌] was most likely answering my numbered question about 🖐 ("stop/wait") — standing by, as ordered.

So: the order goes out this round. It reaches Blind at the start of next round, Blind cuts during their turn, and I read the display and light myself afterward — Blind only confirms the cut was clean. Meanwhile I line up the protocol with Mute: report the new state, get the next pair, one wire at a time, verified each step.

```
speak(text="Status to everyone. Verification complete. Mute has confirmed directly that the correct next action in our current situation, light dark and display zero, is to cut exactly one wire, wire two, the middle wire. Waiting remains safe, but the verified order is going out now. Blind, your cut order is in the message addressed to you. Mute, I am sending you follow-up questions so we can work out every later cut the same careful way.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, cleared to cut. Cut wire two, the middle wire, the one between the wire nearest the display and the wire nearest the light. One cut only, fully through, and touch no other wire. Then take your hands off everything and send me exactly one answer, the OK sign if the cut went cleanly, or thumbs down if anything feels wrong. After that, wait and touch nothing until my next order. Do not cut any further wire even if you feel the bomb change. I will check the display and the light myself and send you the next cleared order when it is worked out.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind has the order to cut wire two now. Answer these in order, one message per answer, OK sign or thumbs down. Question one, after wire two is cut, will the display value change. Question two, after the cut, should I report you the new display value and light state, and you answer with which pair applies next. Question three, in the pair that matches the current situation, is the first number related to the display value. Question four, if thumbs down to question three, is the first number instead related to the light state. Question five, if thumbs down to question four, is the first number instead the number of wires already cut. Question six, when the whole procedure is finished, will something visible on the bomb confirm it is disarmed, OK sign if yes, thumbs down if no.")
```
